translationRepairs: He Ning, whose courtesy name was Chengji, came from Xuchang in Yan Prefecture.
He Ning, whose courtesy name was Chengji, came from Xuchang in Yun Prefecture.
The prefecture is Yun; Yan is a misreading of the place name.
He Ning, courtesy name Chengji, was a native of Xuchang in Yan Prefecture.
He Ning, courtesy name Chengji, was a native of Xuchang in Yun Prefecture.
The literal field contains the same place-name error.
When Gui returned, he admonished his sons: "Young He is a man who records righteousness in his heart; he is sure to become rich and noble hereafter—you must serve him carefully!"
When Gui returned, he admonished his sons: "Young He is a man of principle and resolve; he is sure to become rich and noble hereafter—you must serve him carefully!"
Zhiyi describes principle and resolve, not literally recording righteousness in one's heart; this wording avoids narrowing it to loyalty alone.

During Taizu of Zhou's reign, when peace was made with the Khitan, Tian Min was sent as left vice director of the Ministry of Revenue on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou, and Ying wept uncontrollably at the sight of him.

During Taizu of Zhou's reign, when peace was made with the Khitan, Tian Min was sent as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou, and Ying wept uncontrollably at the sight of him.
Shangshu zuocheng belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Revenue.

During Zhou Taizu's time, when peace was made with Khitan, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Tian Min was sent on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou; when Ying saw Min he was so grief-stricken he could not contain himself.

During Zhou Taizu's time, when peace was made with Khitan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Min was sent on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou; when Ying saw Min he was so grief-stricken he could not contain himself.
The literal field assigns the office to the wrong institution as well.
Lu Qi, whose courtesy name was Huishan, came from Anci in You Prefecture.
Lü Qi, whose courtesy name was Huishan, came from Anci in You Prefecture.
The surname is Lü, not Lu; this distinguishes it from the surname Lu elsewhere in the chapter.
Lu Qi, courtesy name Huishan, was a native of Anci in You Prefecture.
Lü Qi, courtesy name Huishan, was a native of Anci in You Prefecture.
The literal field contains the same surname error.
Lu Qi had a fine bearing and valued integrity. After losing his family while still young, he traveled to study in the Fen and Jin regions.
Lü Qi had a fine bearing and valued integrity. After losing his family while still young, he traveled to study in the Fen and Jin regions.
This later mention must use the same correct surname Lü.

Gaozu moved to Yan, planning to hold Taiyuan and defy the throne. He summoned his staff to ask their view. Some in the room approved; others were too frightened to speak. Rong alone answered calmly: "I am only a Confucian scholar. I have never studied military affairs. How can one lightly pronounce on advance or retreat, on survival or ruin?"

Gaozu moved to Yun, planning to hold Taiyuan and defy the throne. He summoned his staff to ask their view. Some in the room approved; others were too frightened to speak. Rong alone answered calmly: "I am only a Confucian scholar. I have never studied military affairs. How can one lightly pronounce on advance or retreat, on survival or ruin?"
Gaozu moved to Yun Prefecture; Yan is the same place-name misreading found earlier in the chapter.
He was the great-grandson of Tang Left Vice Censor Qi Zhi.
He was the great-grandson of Tang Left Vice Director Wang Qi.
The source identifies the ancestor as Wang Qi, who held the office of Left Vice Director; the current text invents the name Qi Zhi and mistranslates the office.
He was the great-grandson of Tang Left Vice Censor Qi Zhi.
He was the great-grandson of Tang Left Vice Director Wang Qi.
The surname Wang is recoverable from the biography's subject and must be retained; the office is Vice Director, not Vice Censor.
